name: Gambeson
effect: A quilted coat of layered linen or wool, worn alone or beneath heavier armor.

name: Brigandine
effect: Small overlapping metal plates riveted beneath a fitted coat of stout fabric or leather.

name: Mail
effect: A flexible shirt of interlinked iron rings that protects against cuts and thrusts.

name: Half Plate
effect: A mixed harness of shaped steel plates and lighter protection at the joints and limbs.

name: Plate
effect: A full articulated harness of fitted steel plates, made for a wealthy and well-equipped warrior.

name: Padded Barding
effect: Quilted cloth coverings protect a mount from glancing blows without burdening it with metal.

name: Mail Barding
effect: Linked iron rings drape a mount’s vulnerable body, often over a padded underlayer.

name: Plate Barding
effect: Shaped steel plates shield a warhorse’s head and body, an imposing battlefield sight.
